properties.natural_language: All data received via Message sent to gossip network from EXT-SYNC-COMMITTEE-PEER-P2P must be validated before processing. All sync committee messages must be validated: (1) sender is in current sync committee, (2) signature is valid over the correct beacon block root, (3) message timing is within acceptable window per SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS.
If input from EXT-SYNC-COMMITTEE-PEER-P2P via Message sent to gossip network fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Compute Sync Message Due Time can execute, the system must be in Slot Start.
After Compute Sync Message Due Time completes, the system must transition to Sync Message Due with all state invariants preserved.
Before Broadcast Sync Committee Message can execute, the system must be in Sync Message Due.

All data received via Contribution broadcast complete from EXT-AGGREGATION-PEER-P2P must be validated before processing. Aggregated contributions must be validated: (1) aggregation bits and signatures are consistent, (2) included individual messages are valid, (3) submission timing is within CONTRIBUTION_DUE_BPS window.
If input from EXT-AGGREGATION-PEER-P2P via Contribution broadcast complete fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Compute Contribution Due Time can execute, the system must be in Sync Messages Collected.
After Compute Contribution Due Time completes, the system must transition to Contribution Submission Due with all state invariants preserved.
Before Submit Sync Committee Contribution can execute, the system must be in Contribution Submission Due.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-ALTAIR-FC-01): SYNC_MESSAGE_DUE_BPS and CONTRIBUTION_DUE_BPS values are not specified in this document — the system must enforce: Assume these are defined in a configuration or constants file referenced by the spec. Values determine fraction of slot duration for timing.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-ALTAIR-FC-02): Full fork choice algorithm modifications beyond timing helpers are not detailed; spec states 'all prior functionality from Phase0 is inherited' — the system must enforce: Assume Altair fork choice inherits all Phase0 fork choice logic (LMD-GHOST, justified/finalized checkpoints) and only adds sync committee timing.

The system assumes: Nodes have reasonably synchronized clocks to coordinate slot-relative timing for sync messages and contributions. If violated: Desynchronized clocks could cause sync committee messages to arrive outside expected windows, reducing participation rates or causing message rejection

The system assumes: Phase0 fork choice implementation is fully correct and available as a base for Altair modifications. If violated: Bugs in inherited Phase0 fork choice would propagate to Altair, potentially affecting consensus safety

All data received via Operator submits consolidation request from EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR-VIA-TX must be validated before processing. Full validation required: (1) source address is 20 bytes, source/target pubkeys are 48 bytes each, (2) fee payment covers computed exponential fee, (3) queue has not exceeded 262,144 capacity limit. Requests exceeding capacity are discarded without refund.
If input from EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR-VIA-TX via Operator submits consolidation request fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Validate Consolidation Request Format can execute, the system must be in Consolidation Request Submitted.
After Validate Consolidation Request Format completes, Compute Consolidation Fee must proceed as specified by: Calculate required fee.
After Compute Consolidation Fee completes, the system must transition to Consolidation Fee Computed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Fee Payment can execute, the system must be in Consolidation Fee Computed.
After Validate Fee Payment completes, the system must transition to Consolidation Request Queued with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Fee Payment completes, the system must transition to Request Rejected - Insufficient Fee with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Fee Payment completes, the system must transition to Request Rejected - Queue Full with all state invariants preserved.
Before Invoke System Call can execute, the system must be in Block Execution Ending.
After Invoke System Call completes, the system must transition to System Call Executing with all state invariants preserved.
After Invoke System Call completes, the system must transition to No Code at Predeploy Address with all state invariants preserved.
Before Process Consolidation Batch can execute, the system must be in System Call Executing.
After Process Consolidation Batch completes, the system must transition to Consolidations Processed with all state invariants preserved.
After System Call Executing completes, System Call Failed must proceed as specified by: System call fails - block invalid.
Data from external entity EXT-BEACON-CHAIN via Receive validator balance from beacon state must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Validate Minimum Activation Balance can execute, the system must be in Validator Balance Received.
After Validate Minimum Activation Balance completes, the system must transition to Balance Below Minimum with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Minimum Activation Balance completes, Compute Effective Balance must proceed as specified by: Balance >= 32 ETH.
After Compute Effective Balance completes, the system must transition to Effective Balance Computed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Compounding Withdrawal Prefix can execute, the system must be in Effective Balance Computed.
After Check Compounding Withdrawal Prefix completes, the system must transition to Compounding Rewards Enabled with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Compounding Withdrawal Prefix completes, the system must transition to Standard Rewards Mode with all state invariants preserved.

All data received via Operator requests validator exit from EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR-EXIT must be validated before processing. Exit requests must be validated against validator registry. Weight-based churn limiting (256 ETH initial limit) must correctly handle partial exits and deferred processing. Large validator exits (up to 2048 ETH) must not bypass churn limits.
If input from EXT-VALIDATOR-OPERATOR-EXIT via Operator requests validator exit fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Compute Exit Weight can execute, the system must be in Validator Exit Request Received.
After Compute Exit Weight completes, Check Epoch Churn Limit must proceed as specified by: Check against epoch churn limit.
After Check Epoch Churn Limit completes, the system must transition to Exit Within Churn Limit with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Epoch Churn Limit completes, the system must transition to Exit Deferred with all state invariants preserved.
Before Process Partial Exit can execute, the system must be in Exit Deferred.
After Exit Within Churn Limit completes, Exit Processed must proceed as specified by: Exit fully processed this epoch.
After Process Partial Exit completes, the system must transition to Exit Processed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Update Excess Counter can execute, the system must be in Excess Requests Tracked.
After Update Excess Counter completes, Compute Consolidation Base Fee must proceed as specified by: Calculate new base fee.
After Compute Consolidation Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Fee Increased with all state invariants preserved.
After Compute Consolidation Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Fee Decreased with all state invariants preserved.
After Compute Consolidation Base Fee completes, the system must transition to Fee at Minimum with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7251-01): The specification mentions requests exceeding 262,144 capacity are 'discarded without fee refunds' but does not specify how users are notified of this failure. — the system must enforce: Assume the transaction succeeds (fee is taken) but the consolidation request is silently dropped. Users must monitor queue state separately.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7251-02): The term 'surplus deferred' for exits is not precisely defined in terms of queue ordering and priority. — the system must enforce: Assume deferred exits are queued in FIFO order and processed in subsequent epochs as churn budget allows.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP7251-03): The 30M gas limit for system calls is described as 'excluded from block limits' but interaction with EIP-1559 dynamics is unclear. — the system must enforce: Assume system call gas is completely separate from user transaction gas and does not affect base fee calculations.

The system assumes: The predeploy contract at 0x0000BBdDc7CE488642fb579F8B00f3a590007251 is correctly deployed and immutable.. If violated: If the predeploy contract is missing or compromised, all blocks would be invalid or consolidation requests could be manipulated.

The system assumes: An attacker cannot spam consolidation requests fast enough to fill the 262,144 queue and block legitimate requests.. If violated: Queue DoS attack where malicious actors fill the queue, causing legitimate consolidation requests to be discarded without refund.

The system assumes: The exponential fee mechanism provides sufficient economic disincentive against spam during high demand.. If violated: If fee increases are insufficient, well-funded attackers could still economically grief the consolidation system.

The system assumes: Large validators with 2048 ETH effective balance operate with equivalent uptime and reliability as 32 ETH validators.. If violated: Concentrated slashing risk if large validators have correlated failures, potentially affecting network security invariants.

All data received via Transaction submitted via RPC or P2P from EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER-RPC must be validated before processing. Blob-specific validation required: (1) blob gas within protocol limit, (2) max_fee_per_blob_gas >= current blob base fee, (3) versioned hash has correct 0x01 prefix and 32-byte length with valid KZG correspondence, (4) blob data actually present, (5) contract creation prohibited for Type 3.
If input from EXT-BLOB-SUBMITTER-RPC via Transaction submitted via RPC or P2P fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Decode Transaction Type can execute, the system must be in Transaction Received.
After Decode Transaction Type completes, the system must transition to Transaction Type Valid with all state invariants preserved.
After Decode Transaction Type completes, the system must transition to Transaction Type Error with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Contract Creation Validity can execute, the system must be in Transaction Type Valid.
After Check Contract Creation Validity completes, the system must transition to Contract Creation Error with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Max Fee Per Gas can execute, the system must be in Transaction Fees Pending Validation.
After Validate Max Fee Per Gas completes, the system must transition to Insufficient Max Fee Error with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Max Fee Per Gas completes, the system must transition to Max Fee Valid with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Priority Fee can execute, the system must be in Max Fee Valid.
After Validate Priority Fee completes, the system must transition to Priority Fee Error with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Priority Fee completes, the system must transition to All Fees Valid with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Blob Gas Limit can execute, the system must be in Blob Transaction Pending Validation.
After Validate Blob Gas Limit completes, the system must transition to Blob Gas Limit Exceeded with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Blob Gas Limit completes, the system must transition to Blob Gas Within Limit with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Blob Fee can execute, the system must be in Blob Gas Within Limit.
After Validate Blob Fee completes, the system must transition to Insufficient Blob Fee Error with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Blob Fee completes, Validate Versioned Hash must proceed as specified by: Continue to hash validation.
After Validate Versioned Hash completes, the system must transition to Invalid Versioned Hash Error with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Versioned Hash completes, Check Blob Data Presence must proceed as specified by: Verify blob data exists.
After Check Blob Data Presence completes, the system must transition to No Blob Data Error with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Blob Data Presence completes, the system must transition to Blob Validation Complete with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Init Code Size can execute, the system must be in Contract Creation Transaction.
After Validate Init Code Size completes, the system must transition to Init Code Too Large Error with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Init Code Size completes, the system must transition to Init Code Size Valid with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CANCUN-EXC-01): TransactionTypeContractCreationError references 'a transaction type that prohibits it' without specifying which types prohibit contract creation. — the system must enforce: Assume blob transactions (type 3) prohibit contract creation based on EIP-4844 specification. Requires cross-reference with transaction type rules.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-CANCUN-EXC-02): InvalidBlobVersionedHashError does not specify all validity conditions for versioned hashes. — the system must enforce: Assume validity requires: correct version byte prefix (0x01), correct hash length (32 bytes), and valid KZG commitment correspondence.

The system assumes: Exception types assume the transaction data has been correctly deserialized before validation begins.. If violated: Malformed RLP data could bypass type-specific validation if deserialization errors are not caught first.

The system assumes: The system assumes attackers cannot forge valid blob versioned hashes without possessing the corresponding blob data.. If violated: Hash forgery could allow inclusion of invalid or missing blob data in blocks.

The system assumes: Fee validation assumes block base fee is correctly computed from parent block parameters.. If violated: Incorrect base fee calculation could allow transactions with insufficient fees or reject valid transactions.
Before Pop Stack Arguments can execute, the system must be in CREATE2 Opcode Invoked.
After Pop Stack Arguments completes, the system must transition to Arguments Loaded with all state invariants preserved.
Before Read Init Code from Memory can execute, the system must be in Arguments Loaded.
After Read Init Code from Memory completes, the system must transition to Init Code Loaded with all state invariants preserved.
Before Compute and Deduct Hash Cost can execute, the system must be in Init Code Loaded.
After Compute and Deduct Hash Cost completes, the system must transition to Hash Cost Deducted with all state invariants preserved.
Before Compute Deterministic Address can execute, the system must be in Hash Cost Deducted.
After Compute Deterministic Address completes, the system must transition to Target Address Computed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Address Collision can execute, the system must be in Target Address Computed.
After Check Address Collision completes, the system must transition to No Address Collision with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Address Collision completes, the system must transition to Address Collision Detected with all state invariants preserved.
Before Execute Init Code can execute, the system must be in No Address Collision.
After Execute Init Code completes, the system must transition to Contract Deployed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Push Address to Stack can execute, the system must be in Contract Deployed.
After Push Address to Stack completes, the system must transition to CREATE2 Complete with all state invariants preserved.
After Address Collision Detected completes, CREATE2 Failed must proceed as specified by: Deployment aborted.
Before Deduct CREATE Base Cost can execute, the system must be in Gas Available for CREATE2.
After Deduct CREATE Base Cost completes, the system must transition to Base Cost Deducted with all state invariants preserved.
Before Calculate Init Code Hash Cost can execute, the system must be in Base Cost Deducted.
After Calculate Init Code Hash Cost completes, Deduct Hash Cost must proceed as specified by: Charge for hashing.
After Deduct Hash Cost completes, the system must transition to Hash Cost Deducted with all state invariants preserved.
Before Deduct Memory Expansion Cost can execute, the system must be in Hash Cost Deducted.
After Deduct Memory Expansion Cost completes, the system must transition to Memory Cost Deducted with all state invariants preserved.
After Deduct CREATE Base Cost completes, the system must transition to Out of Gas with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Account Nonce can execute, the system must be in Computed Address to Validate.
After Check Account Nonce completes, the system must transition to Nonce is Zero with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Account Nonce completes, the system must transition to Nonce is Non-Zero with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Account Code can execute, the system must be in Nonce is Zero.
After Check Account Code completes, the system must transition to Code is Empty with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Account Code completes, the system must transition to Code Exists with all state invariants preserved.
After Code is Empty completes, Address Safe for Deployment must proceed as specified by: Address available.
After Nonce is Non-Zero completes, Address Collision Error must proceed as specified by: Collision detected.
After Code Exists completes, Address Collision Error must proceed as specified by: Collision detected.
Before Throw Invalid Opcode Error can execute, the system must be in Address Collision Error.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1014-01): The behavior when CREATE2 is called with zero endowment but the target address has non-zero balance (from previous SELFDESTRUCT) is not explicitly defined. — the system must enforce: Assume CREATE2 proceeds if nonce is zero and code is empty, regardless of existing balance at the target address.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1014-02): The specification does not clarify whether the 0xff prefix is included before or after RLP encoding considerations. — the system must enforce: Assume 0xff is a raw single byte (not RLP encoded) concatenated directly with the other preimage components.

The system assumes: The keccak256 hash function is collision-resistant, making it infeasible to find two different init codes that produce the same deployment address.. If violated: Attackers could deploy malicious contracts at addresses expected to contain legitimate code, enabling contract impersonation attacks.

The system assumes: An attacker cannot predict or control the salt value chosen by legitimate deployers.. If violated: If attackers can front-run CREATE2 deployments with known salts, they could deploy malicious contracts at expected addresses before the legitimate deployment.

The system assumes: The EIP-684 collision check is always performed atomically before any state modification.. If violated: Race conditions in collision checking could allow deployment to addresses that should be blocked.
Data from external entity EXT-EIP-AUTHOR via Author creates and submits EIP draft must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Present at AllCoreDevs can execute, the system must be in EIP in Draft State.
After Present at AllCoreDevs completes, the system must transition to EIP Under Discussion with all state invariants preserved.
Before Core Devs Reach Consensus can execute, the system must be in EIP Under Discussion.
After Core Devs Reach Consensus completes, the system must transition to Eligible for Inclusion with all state invariants preserved.
After Core Devs Reach Consensus completes, the system must transition to EIP in Draft State with all state invariants preserved.
After Eligible for Inclusion completes, Implementation Phase must proceed as specified by: Client teams begin implementation.
After Implementation Phase completes, Testing Phase must proceed as specified by: Implementation PRs merged for testing.
After Testing Phase completes, Accepted for Fork must proceed as specified by: Testing successful, fork assignment.
After Accepted for Fork completes, Deployed on Mainnet must proceed as specified by: Hard fork activates at scheduled block.
Before Discuss EIP Proposal can execute, the system must be in AllCoreDevs Call Scheduled.
After Discuss EIP Proposal completes, the system must transition to Feedback Collected with all state invariants preserved.
Before Assess Rough Consensus can execute, the system must be in Feedback Collected.
After Assess Rough Consensus completes, the system must transition to Consensus Exists with all state invariants preserved.
After Assess Rough Consensus completes, the system must transition to No Consensus with all state invariants preserved.
Before Document Decision can execute, the system must be in Consensus Exists.
Before Document Decision can execute, the system must be in No Consensus.
After Document Decision completes, the system must transition to Decision Recorded with all state invariants preserved.

All data received via Begin eligibility validation from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P must be validated before processing. Full block validation required: header fields, gas limit bounds, PoW/PoS validity, transaction execution correctness, state root verification. All data from peers is potentially malicious.
If input from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P via Begin eligibility validation fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
After Check Conceptual Support completes, the system must transition to Conceptually Supported with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Conceptual Support completes, the system must transition to Validation Failed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Implementation Willingness can execute, the system must be in Conceptually Supported.
After Check Implementation Willingness completes, the system must transition to Implementation Acceptable with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Implementation Willingness completes, the system must transition to Validation Failed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Check Documentation Link can execute, the system must be in Implementation Acceptable.
After Check Documentation Link completes, the system must transition to Fully Validated with all state invariants preserved.
After Check Documentation Link completes, the system must transition to Validation Failed with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2378-01): The term 'rough consensus' is used without a precise definition of what constitutes sufficient agreement. — the system must enforce: Assume rough consensus means a clear majority of active core developers agree, without formal voting requirements. Interpret as IETF-style rough consensus.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2378-02): The specification does not define a process for revoking eligibility once granted. — the system must enforce: Assume eligibility can be revoked through the same ACD consensus process that granted it, though this is not documented.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2378-03): The phrase 'well written PRs' for implementation acceptance is subjective. — the system must enforce: Assume this refers to PRs that follow client codebase conventions, include tests, and properly implement the specification.

The system assumes: Core developers participating in ACD calls represent the interests of the Ethereum ecosystem broadly.. If violated: Governance capture could lead to harmful EIPs being approved for inclusion.
The system assumes: ACD meeting notes accurately capture the consensus decision and reasoning.. If violated: Inaccurate notes could misrepresent decisions, leading to disputes about EIP status.

The system assumes: The EIP process continues to function with volunteer participation from client developers.. If violated: If key client teams stop participating, the governance process could break down.

All data received via User submits Type 1 transaction for signing from EXT-USER-DAPP-TYPE1 must be validated before processing. Conversion must correctly map gas_price to both max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas. Access list must be preserved unchanged. Chain ID must be maintained. Type field updated from 0x1 to 0x2. Incorrect conversion could alter transaction economics.
If input from EXT-USER-DAPP-TYPE1 via User submits Type 1 transaction for signing fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Detect Transaction Type can execute, the system must be in Type 1 Transaction Submitted.
After Detect Transaction Type completes, the system must transition to Type 1 Transaction Detected with all state invariants preserved.
Before Extract Access List can execute, the system must be in Type 1 Transaction Detected.
After Extract Access List completes, Extract Gas Price must proceed as specified by: Extract gas parameters.
After Extract Gas Price completes, Convert to Type 2 Transaction must proceed as specified by: Begin conversion.
After Convert to Type 2 Transaction completes, Set Type Field to 0x2 must proceed as specified by: Update type to 0x2.
After Set Type Field to 0x2 completes, Set Max Fee Fields must proceed as specified by: Convert gas price to max fees.
After Set Max Fee Fields completes, the system must transition to Type 2 Transaction Ready with all state invariants preserved.
Before Sign Type 2 Transaction can execute, the system must be in Type 2 Transaction Ready.
After Sign Type 2 Transaction completes, the system must transition to Transaction Signed with all state invariants preserved.
Before Map Access List (Unchanged) can execute, the system must be in Type 1 Transaction Fields.
After Map Access List (Unchanged) completes, Remove gas_price Field must proceed as specified by: Handle gas_price removal.
After Remove gas_price Field completes, Create max_fee_per_gas must proceed as specified by: Create replacement field.
After Create max_fee_per_gas completes, Create max_priority_fee_per_gas must proceed as specified by: Create priority fee field.
After Create max_priority_fee_per_gas completes, Update Type to 0x2 must proceed as specified by: Update type identifier.
After Update Type to 0x2 completes, the system must transition to Type 2 Transaction Fields with all state invariants preserved.
Before Interpret as Maximum Fee can execute, the system must be in Legacy gas_price Value.
After Interpret as Maximum Fee completes, Derive Priority Fee must proceed as specified by: Calculate priority fee.
After Derive Priority Fee completes, the system must transition to EIP-1559 Fee Structure with all state invariants preserved.
After EIP-1559 Fee Structure completes, User Receives EIP-1559 Benefits must proceed as specified by: User now has EIP-1559 transaction.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP3709-01): The specification does not define exactly how gas_price should be mapped to max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas — the system must enforce: Assume both max_fee_per_gas and max_priority_fee_per_gas are set equal to the original gas_price value.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP3709-02): The specification says wallets 'MUST' convert but doesn't specify handling if user explicitly requests Type 1 — the system must enforce: Assume the conversion is automatic and transparent; wallets should not offer option to preserve Type 1 format.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP3709-03): The specification doesn't address what happens to the chain_id field during conversion — the system must enforce: Assume chain_id is preserved unchanged during the Type 1 to Type 2 conversion.
The system assumes: The network supports EIP-1559 and Type 2 transactions (London fork or later). If violated: Converted Type 2 transactions would be rejected by pre-London nodes
The system assumes: Users submitting Type 1 transactions will accept automatic conversion to Type 2. If violated: Users expecting Type 1 behavior might be confused by Type 2 fee mechanics

The system assumes: The wallet performs the conversion correctly without modifying transaction intent. If violated: Incorrect conversion could result in transactions with different gas economics than intended
The system assumes: No security benefit is lost by deprecating Type 1 in favor of Type 2. If violated: Potential edge cases where Type 1 offered security properties not present in Type 2

All data received via Peer A initiates connection to Peer B from EXT-PEER-RLPX-INITIATOR must be validated before processing. Auth packet must be decryptable via ECIES with recipient's static key. Required fields (signature, initiator-pubk, initiator-nonce) must be present. Version mismatches and extra RLP elements are tolerated per EIP-8 but must not cause crashes or buffer overflows. Random padding (100-300 bytes) should use cryptographically secure randomness.
If input from EXT-PEER-RLPX-INITIATOR via Peer A initiates connection to Peer B fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Generate Auth Packet can execute, the system must be in Handshake Initiated.
After Generate Auth Packet completes, the system must transition to Auth Packet Sent with all state invariants preserved.
Before Decrypt Auth Packet can execute, the system must be in Auth Packet Sent.
After Decrypt Auth Packet completes, Parse Auth Body (Tolerant) must proceed as specified by: Decrypted plaintext ready for parsing.
After Parse Auth Body (Tolerant) completes, the system must transition to Auth Packet Validated with all state invariants preserved.
Before Generate Ack Packet can execute, the system must be in Auth Packet Validated.
After Generate Ack Packet completes, the system must transition to Ack Packet Sent with all state invariants preserved.
After Ack Packet Sent completes, Handshake Complete must proceed as specified by: Both parties ready for encrypted communication.

All data received via Remote peer sends hello packet from EXT-REMOTE-PEER-HELLO must be validated before processing. Hello packets parsed with forward-compatible tolerance. Version mismatches ignored. Capability advertisements must not be trusted without further protocol-level validation. Additional list elements and trailing data ignored safely.
If input from EXT-REMOTE-PEER-HELLO via Remote peer sends hello packet fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Parse Hello (Forward-Compatible) can execute, the system must be in Hello Packet Received.
After Parse Hello (Forward-Compatible) completes, the system must transition to Hello Accepted with all state invariants preserved.
Before Send Hello Response can execute, the system must be in Hello Accepted.
After Send Hello Response completes, the system must transition to Peer Connection Established with all state invariants preserved.

All data received via Receive discovery UDP packet from EXT-DISCOVERY-PEER-UDP must be validated before processing. Packets must not exceed 1280 bytes. Unknown packet types silently discarded. Known types (ping/pong/findnode/neighbours) processed with tolerant RLP parsing. UDP source addresses are spoofable — no authentication at transport level.
If input from EXT-DISCOVERY-PEER-UDP via Receive discovery UDP packet fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Validate Packet Size can execute, the system must be in Discovery Packet Received.
After Validate Packet Size completes, Parse Discovery (Tolerant) must proceed as specified by: Size valid, begin parsing.
After Parse Discovery (Tolerant) completes, the system must transition to Known Packet Type with all state invariants preserved.
After Parse Discovery (Tolerant) completes, the system must transition to Unknown Packet Type with all state invariants preserved.
Before Process Discovery Packet can execute, the system must be in Known Packet Type.
Before Silent Discard can execute, the system must be in Unknown Packet Type.

All data received via Begin validation from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P must be validated before processing. Full block validation required: header fields, gas limit bounds, PoW/PoS validity, transaction execution correctness, state root verification. All data from peers is potentially malicious.
If input from EXT-PEER-VIA-P2P via Begin validation fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
After Check Required Fields completes, Skip Version Check must proceed as specified by: Required fields present.
After Check Required Fields completes, the system must transition to Validation Failed with all state invariants preserved.
After Skip Version Check completes, Ignore Extra Elements must proceed as specified by: Version check bypassed.
After Ignore Extra Elements completes, the system must transition to Validation Passed with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP8-01): The recommended padding range of '100-300 bytes random' does not specify the distribution or entropy requirements for the random data. — the system must enforce: Assume cryptographically secure random bytes are required to prevent traffic analysis attacks.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP8-02): The phrase 'silently discarded' for unknown packet types does not specify if this should be logged or counted for rate limiting. — the system must enforce: Assume silent discard means no error response to sender, but local logging may occur for debugging.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP8-03): No specification for handling simultaneous connection attempts between two peers using different protocol formats (v4 vs EIP-8). — the system must enforce: Assume the receiving node determines format based on packet structure and responds in the same format.

The system assumes: The ECIES encryption with recipient's static public key ensures only the intended recipient can decrypt auth/ack packets.. If violated: Man-in-the-middle attacks could intercept and forge handshake packets.
The system assumes: Attackers cannot generate valid signatures without the initiator's private key.. If violated: Connection hijacking or impersonation attacks possible.
The system assumes: All future protocol versions will maintain backward compatibility with the RLP structure requirements.. If violated: Forward compatibility breaks, negating the purpose of EIP-8.
The system assumes: The 1280 byte discovery packet limit is sufficient for all current and future discovery message types.. If violated: Protocol extensions may be blocked by size constraints.

All data received via dApp calls wallet_requestPermissions from EXT-DAPP-WALLET-RPC must be validated before processing. Permission system must: (1) correctly identify invoker origin without spoofing, (2) present clear consent UI resistant to clickjacking, (3) enforce caveat restrictions on method calls, (4) validate URLs against SSRF (scheme and port whitelisting), (5) filter permissions by invoker on query. Error 4001 returned on user rejection per EIP-1193.
If input from EXT-DAPP-WALLET-RPC via dApp calls wallet_requestPermissions fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.

All data received via User clicks approve from EXT-END-USER must be validated before processing. User must be shown clear, accurate information about what they are approving. Phishing-resistant UI required.
If input from EXT-END-USER via User clicks approve fails validation, the system must reject it without altering internal state.
Before Prompt User for Consent can execute, the system must be in Permission Request Pending.
After Prompt User for Consent completes, the system must transition to User Rejected Permissions with all state invariants preserved.
Before Grant Permission can execute, the system must be in User Approved Permissions.
After Grant Permission completes, the system must transition to Permission Granted with all state invariants preserved.
Before Throw Error 4001 can execute, the system must be in User Rejected Permissions.
While in dApp Connected to Wallet: dApp has established connection to wallet but has no permissions.
Data from external entity EXT-DAPP-CALLER via dApp calls restricted method must be treated as untrusted and validated.
Before Check if Permission Required can execute, the system must be in RPC Call Received.
After Check if Permission Required completes, the system must transition to Permission Not Required with all state invariants preserved.
After Check if Permission Required completes, the system must transition to Permission Required with all state invariants preserved.
Before Lookup Permission can execute, the system must be in Permission Required.
After Lookup Permission completes, the system must transition to Permission Found with all state invariants preserved.
After Lookup Permission completes, the system must transition to Permission Not Found with all state invariants preserved.
Before Validate Caveats can execute, the system must be in Permission Found.
After Validate Caveats completes, the system must transition to Method Execution Allowed with all state invariants preserved.
After Validate Caveats completes, the system must transition to Method Execution Denied with all state invariants preserved.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2255-01): The term 'invoker' is defined as a URI but the exact format and validation rules for the invoker string are not specified. — the system must enforce: Assume invoker is the origin URL of the dApp (e.g., 'https://example.com') following web origin conventions.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2255-02): The specification does not define how permissions are persisted or when they expire. — the system must enforce: Assume permissions persist until explicitly revoked or wallet is reset; implementers may add expiration caveats.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2255-03): The 'date' field in RequestedPermission is optional and its purpose is unclear - is it grant time or expiration time? — the system must enforce: Assume 'date' is the Unix timestamp when the permission was granted, used for auditing purposes.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2255-04): The term 'caveat' is used without explicit enumeration of all valid caveat types. — the system must enforce: Assume caveats are extensible and implementation-specific; 'requiredMethods' is one example shown.

The system assumes: The wallet correctly identifies the invoker (dApp origin) without spoofing.. If violated: A malicious dApp could impersonate a trusted dApp and inherit its permissions, enabling unauthorized access.

The system assumes: Attackers cannot bypass the permission check by directly calling internal wallet methods.. If violated: Privilege escalation allowing attackers to execute restricted methods without user consent.

The system assumes: The user interface for permission consent is not susceptible to clickjacking or UI redressing attacks.. If violated: Users could be tricked into approving permissions without understanding what they're granting.

The system assumes: Permission prompts clearly display requested capabilities and caveats in a user-understandable way.. If violated: Users may grant permissions without understanding the security implications, leading to over-permissioning.

The system assumes: The wallet's permission storage is protected from tampering by malicious extensions or local software.. If violated: Attackers could inject permissions without user consent, enabling unauthorized dApp access.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2718-01): Behavior for first byte value 0xff (reserved) is not specified — the system must enforce: Assume transactions starting with 0xff are rejected as invalid until a future EIP defines their meaning.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2718-02): The phrase 'SHOULD include the TransactionType as the first byte of the signed data' is a recommendation, not requirement — the system must enforce: Assume compliant implementations MUST include the type byte in signed data to prevent cross-type signature reuse attacks, treating this as a de facto requirement.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP2718-03): The boundary between typed [0x00-0x7f] and legacy [0xc0-0xfe] transactions leaves gap [0x80-0xbf] undefined — the system must enforce: Assume bytes in range [0x80-0xbf] are invalid and transactions should be rejected. This range would be valid RLP list starts that are too short to be valid legacy transactions.

The system assumes: New transaction types will be introduced only through the EIP process with proper security review. If violated: Malicious or poorly designed transaction types could introduce consensus vulnerabilities or security holes

The system assumes: An attacker cannot create a valid signature for a different transaction type using the same signed data. If violated: Signature replay attacks across transaction types, allowing transactions to be executed with unintended semantics

The system assumes: All nodes on the network support the same set of activated transaction types at any given block height. If violated: Network partition or consensus failures if nodes disagree on valid transaction types for a block

The system assumes: Wallet software will correctly implement type-specific signing to include the type byte. If violated: Users could sign transactions that are vulnerable to type-confusion attacks if wallets omit type byte from signed data

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1803-01): The specification does not clarify whether assemblers should accept both old and new mnemonic names or only the new ones. — the system must enforce: Assume assemblers should accept both old and new names for backward compatibility during a transition period.

Despite ambiguity (AMB-EIP1803-02): The term 'ABORT' for opcode 0xfe is described as replacement for 'INVALID' but the semantic difference between abort and invalid behavior is not specified. — the system must enforce: Assume ABORT has identical semantics to INVALID - both cause the EVM to halt and consume all remaining gas.

The system assumes: All EVM tooling (compilers, debuggers, disassemblers) will be updated to recognize the new mnemonic names.. If violated: Tooling fragmentation where some tools use old names and others use new names, causing confusion in contract auditing and debugging.

The system assumes: Documentation and educational materials will be updated to reflect the new naming conventions.. If violated: Developer confusion when documentation uses different names than actual tooling, potentially leading to incorrect code or security misunderstandings.
